# Multi-factor authentication

HCP supports multi-factor authentication (MFA) for individual user accounts. Each sign-in method maintains its own MFA configuration. When you add a new sign-in method to your account, configure MFA for that method separately.

| Sign-in method | Management interface | Instructions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| IBMid | MFA is managed through your IBM account. | Refer to the [IBMid MFA documentation](https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/ibmid). |
| GitHub | MFA is managed through your GitHub account. | Refer to [Configuring two-factor authentication](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/securing-your-account-with-two-factor-authentication-2fa) in the GitHub documentation. |
| Email and password | MFA is managed in HCP. | Refer to [Enable MFA](#enable-mfa). |

Changes to MFA affect your access to HashiCorp Developer, Discuss, Events, and the Certification Portal, because the same account is used to access those sites.

## Requirements

You must have one of the following artifacts to [disable MFA](#disable-mfa). 

- Your current OTP from your authenticator app
- Your recovery code
- An active HCP session with **Remember this browser** enabled

If you do not have access to any of the artifacts necessary for disabling MFA, contact [IBM support](https://www.ibm.com/mysupport) to perform a hard reset of your HCP MFA configuration.

## Enable MFA

To enable MFA, complete the following steps.

1. From your user profile menu, click **Account settings**.

   ![Account Settings](/img/docs/account-settings.png 'Account Settings')

1. In **Account settings**, click the **Security** tab.

   ![Security Tab](/img/docs/security-tab.png 'Security Tab')

1. If MFA is not yet enabled, the **Status** displays **Not enabled**. Click **Enable MFA**. The setup process may take up to 10 minutes to complete.

   ![Enable MFA](/img/docs/updated-enable-mfa.png 'Enable MFA')

1. Click **Continue**. HCP redirects you to the sign-in screen to re-authenticate. After you sign back in, the One-Time Password screen appears.

   ![One-Time Password](/img/docs/otp.png 'One-Time Password')

1. Use an authenticator app, such as Google Authenticator, to scan the QR code, then enter the 6-digit code provided by the app and click **Verify**. If you cannot scan the QR code, click the text code link to copy a string you can enter manually into your authenticator app.

1. Record the recovery code and store it in a secure location. You can use the recovery code to sign in if you lose access to your device.

   ![Recovery Code](/img/docs/recovery-code.png 'Recovery Code')

The **Status** changes to **MFA enabled**.

## Disable MFA

To disable MFA, complete the following steps.

1. Click **Account settings**, and then click **Security**. In the **Multi-factor authentication (MFA)** section, click **Disable MFA**.

   ![Disable MFA](/img/docs/disableMFA.png 'Disable MFA')

1. Sign in again using your existing sign-in method, then enter your 6-digit OTP code.

   ![OTP](/img/docs/documentation.png 'OTP')

1. On the **Disable MFA** page, type `DISABLE` to confirm, then click **Disable MFA**.

   ![Disable MFA](/img/docs/updated-disable-mfa.png 'Disable MFA')

## Troubleshooting

If you cannot verify your 6-digit code, the system may be temporarily unavailable.

![QR Error Code](/img/docs/qr-code-error.png 'QR Error code')

Try generating a new OTP. If you cannot access your device, use the recovery code you saved during setup to sign in. The setup process times out after five minutes; if the timeout expires, restart the setup.

If errors persist or you have lost your recovery code, contact [IBM support](https://www.ibm.com/mysupport) to perform a hard reset of your HCP MFA configuration.
